segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod. My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。 我的名字是马可。

segments.en: And my name is Catherine.
segments.zh: 我叫 Catherine。

segments.en: And today we're talking about some very interesting stories.
segments.zh: 今天我们谈论一些非常有趣的故事。

segments.en: We're going to learn some words for stories or tales.
segments.zh: 我们要学一些表示故事或传说的词。

segments.en: But specifically, what kind of stories, Marco?
segments.zh: 但具体来说，什么样的故事，马可？

segments.en: They're popular stories that you hear maybe through emails or maybe in your town there's some particular story about maybe a ghost or many different things that they're kind of hard to believe but that happened a long time ago and people still talk about today.
segments.zh: 它们是些流传很广的故事，你可能通过邮件听说，或者你的镇上就有某个特别的传说，也许是关于鬼魂之类各种各样的东西。这些故事有点让人难以相信，但据说发生在很久以前，人们至今还在谈论。

segments.en: And they're scary.
segments.zh: 而且它们很吓人。

segments.en: Yeah, they're kind of scary.
segments.zh: 是的，它们有点吓人。

segments.en: So let's listen to today's dialogue, hear some interesting stories.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听今天的对话，听听一些有趣的故事。

segments.en: And when we come back, we'll be talking more about what these words and phrases mean.
segments.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将更多地谈论这些单词和短语的含义。

segments.en: Have you read all these crazy things that are going on around the world?
segments.zh: 你看过这些世界各地的离奇传闻吗？

segments.en: What do you mean?
segments.zh: 你是什么意思？

segments.en: I was reading about how some people get tricked or drugged in their hotel rooms and have their organs removed.
segments.zh: 我看到有人说，住酒店的人可能遭人哄骗或下药，器官被摘走。

segments.en: Then they're sold on the black market.
segments.zh: 然后那些器官被拿到黑市贩卖。

segments.en: Don't tell me you actually believe all that.
segments.zh: 你不会真信这些吧？

segments.en: Don't be so gullible. They are just urban legends. They're just stories people make up to scare you.
segments.zh: 别这么轻信，那只是都市传说，都是人们编出来吓人的。

segments.en: Well, I was also reading about how some popular songs have subliminal or even satanic messages if you play them backwards.
segments.zh: 我还看到有人说，把某些流行歌曲倒放，会听到潜意识暗示，甚至撒旦崇拜的信息。

segments.en: Can you believe that?
segments.zh: 你能信吗？

segments.en: You really think an artist or songwriter is going to go through the trouble of putting subliminal or satanic messages in a song?
segments.zh: 你真觉得歌手或词曲作者会费力往歌里藏潜意识暗示或撒旦崇拜信息？

segments.en: Don't be so naive.
segments.zh: 别这么天真。

segments.en: Well maybe you are right.
segments.zh: 也许你说得对。

segments.en: But how about the story about how KFC has rows of headless chickens which are super grown in order to get bigger chickens faster?
segments.zh: 可传说肯德基养着一排排无头鸡，让它们迅速长大，好更快得到大块鸡肉，这又怎么说？

segments.en: Sounds a bit too far-fetched to be true, don't you think?
segments.zh: 听起来也太离谱了，你不觉得吗？

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So let's take a look at Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么让我们来看看语言要点。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So here on Language Takeaway today, we have some words that will help us understand the dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以在今天的语言要点部分，我们有一些词能帮大家理解对话。

segments.en: The first word is drugged.
segments.zh: 第一个词是 drugged。

segments.en: So I was reading about how some people get drugged in their hotel rooms.
segments.zh: 所以我正在阅读一些人如何在他们的酒店房间里被下药。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So if you get drugged, it means that someone gave you some drugs in order to make you sleepy or in order for you to not remember what happened.
segments.zh: 所以如果你被下药了，这意味着有人给了你一些药物，让你昏昏欲睡，或者为了让你不记得发生了什么。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So he was drugged means someone gave him a drug, something that made him go to sleep.
segments.zh: 所以他被下药意味着有人给了他药物，这让他睡着了。

segments.en: Right. And it's not necessarily always a bad thing because obviously if you go to the hospital, the doctor may drug you in order to, you know, so you don't feel so much pain or something.
segments.zh: 对。 而且这不一定总是一件坏事，因为很明显，如果你去医院，医生可能会给你下药，你知道，这样你就不会感到那么痛苦或什么的。

segments.en: Exactly. If you're in an accident, you're in a lot of pain, the doctor drugs you so you don't feel that pain.
segments.zh: 没错。 如果你出事了，你会很痛苦，医生给你药物，这样你就不会感到那种痛苦。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: All right. So he was drugged. This person is drugged.
segments.zh: 好的。 于是他被下药了。 这个人被下药了。

segments.en: And then what happens?
segments.zh: 然后会发生什么？

segments.en: Well, his organs were removed.
segments.zh: 好吧，他的器官被移除了。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So organ, an organ is a noun.
segments.zh: 所以器官，器官是名词。

segments.en: It's a thing.
segments.zh: 这是个东西。

segments.en: Those are actually the things that are inside our body.
segments.zh: 这些实际上是我们体内的东西。

segments.en: Right. So your heart, liver, your pancreas, kidneys, etc.
segments.zh: 对。 所以你的心脏、肝脏、胰腺、肾脏等。

segments.en: These are all organs. And this is basically the category for the part of the body.
segments.zh: 这些都是器官。这基本上是身体各部位的统称。

segments.en: It's anything really inside your body that has a function.
segments.zh: 它是你体内真正有功能的东西。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is supposedly this story is that people, you know, usually tourists, they get tricked or drugged and then they get their organs removed.
segments.zh: 所以这个故事大概是说，人们，你知道，通常是游客，被人骗或被下药，然后器官被摘走。

segments.en: Now what kind of a story is this, Marco?
segments.zh: 现在这是一个什么样的故事，马可？

segments.en: Because it's not just a normal story.
segments.zh: 因为这不仅仅是一个普通的故事。

segments.en: Right. All of these stories that we saw in the dialogue are called urban legends.
segments.zh: 对。 我们在对话中看到的所有这些故事都被称为都市传说。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Urban has to do with cities, right? Legend is a story that may or may not be true.
segments.zh: urban 跟城市有关，对吧？legend 就是可能真、也可能假的故事。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: It comes from a long time ago.
segments.zh: 它来自很久以前。

segments.en: So an urban legend is actually a story that is probably not true that you hear from other people like your friends.
segments.zh: 所以一个都市传说实际上是一个你从其他人那里听到的可能不是真实的故事。

segments.en: That's right. So usually most of these stories fall under this category.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以通常这些故事中的大多数都属于这一类。

segments.en: You know, they're urban legends. You don't really know if they're true, but people say it happened to a friend of theirs from a long time ago or stuff like that.
segments.zh: 你知道，它们是都市传说。 你真的不知道它们是否是真的，但人们说这件事发生在他们很久以前的朋友身上或类似的事情上。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So a friend of a friend of a friend of mine told me that in hotels, sometimes they take your organs.
segments.zh: 所以我一个朋友的朋友的一个朋友告诉我，在酒店里，有时他们会拿走你的器官。

segments.en: Well, obviously that's not right.
segments.zh: 好吧，显然这是不对的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Right. All right. So after that, we have two great adjectives for describing people who like to believe stories like this.
segments.zh: 对。 好的。 所以在那之后，我们有两个很棒的形容词来描述那些喜欢相信这样故事的人。

segments.en: What are those two adjectives?
segments.zh: 这两个形容词是什么？

segments.en: Well, we have the adjective to be gullible and to be naive.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们有两个形容词：to be gullible 和 to be naive。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So they're a little bit different.
segments.zh: 所以它们有点不同。

segments.en: To be gullible means to believe everything that people tell you.
segments.zh: 容易上当受骗意味着相信人们告诉你的一切。

segments.en: Right. So if you're gullible, you pretty much believe anything you see or you hear.
segments.zh: 对。 因此，如果您容易上当受骗，您几乎相信您所看到或听到的任何内容。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So maybe your friend says, did you know Michael Jordan is coming to the office tomorrow?
segments.zh: 所以也许你的朋友说，你知道迈克尔乔丹明天要来办公室吗？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And you believe it, then you're very, very gullible.
segments.zh: 你相信它，那么你非常非常容易上当受骗。

segments.en: Very gullible.
segments.zh: 很容易上当受骗。

segments.en: You believe what people tell you.
segments.zh: 你相信人们告诉你的。

segments.en: But naive is similar.
segments.zh: 但 naive 跟它很像。

segments.en: It's similar, but I guess it has a little bit of a different meaning in the sense that you're not, it's not that you're so gullible, but you wholeheartedly trust people.
segments.zh: 这两个词很像，但我觉得意思还是有点不同：不是说你好骗，而是你全心全意地信任别人。

segments.en: So you're naive, you're innocent.
segments.zh: 所以你很天真，很单纯。

segments.en: You're innocent.
segments.zh: 你很单纯。

segments.en: Maybe you don't have a lot of life experience.
segments.zh: 也许你没有很多生活经验。

segments.en: So you trust people and you can call a person naive. You say, well, he's very naive about these kinds of things.
segments.zh: 所以你相信别人，你可以说一个人天真。 你说，嗯，他对这些事情很天真。

segments.en: I guess that's the main key, right?
segments.zh: 我想这是主要的关键，对吧？

segments.en: Or the main point is that you don't really have too much life experience.
segments.zh: 或者主要的一点是你并没有太多的生活经验。

segments.en: So that's why you're naive.
segments.zh: 所以这就是你天真的原因。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And just be careful because gullible and naive are things that we say about people, but they're not nice things.
segments.zh: 只是要小心，因为 gullible 和 naive 是我们用来评价人的词，但都不是好话。

segments.en: They're not compliments.
segments.zh: 它们不是夸奖的话。

segments.en: Right. So you shouldn't really say it to someone directly like in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 对。 所以你不应该真的像在对话中那样直接对某人说。

segments.en: Exactly. Maybe as a joke, but not seriously.
segments.zh: 没错。 也许是一个笑话，但不是认真的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we have the great adjectives way to describe people.
segments.zh: 所以我们有很好的形容词来形容人。

segments.en: And lastly, we also have something else that how to describe the situation.
segments.zh: 最后，我们还有其他东西来描述这种情况。

segments.en: Maybe it's too farfetched. It's too difficult to believe.
segments.zh: 也许它太牵强了。 太难相信了。

segments.en: So farfetched, this is a great word.
segments.zh: farfetched 是个很棒的词。

segments.en: It means basically that something is very difficult to believe.
segments.zh: 这基本上意味着某事很难相信。

segments.en: Like you say, for example, the story about Michael Jordan.
segments.zh: 就像你说的，例如，关于迈克尔乔丹的故事。

segments.en: Michael Jordan is coming tomorrow.
segments.zh: 迈克尔乔丹明天就要来了。

segments.en: You say, oh, that's pretty farfetched. I don't really think that could happen.
segments.zh: 你说，哦，这很牵强。 我真的不认为这会发生。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So something that is farfetched is difficult to happen or very, very unlikely to happen.
segments.zh: 因此，牵强的事情很难发生或非常非常不可能发生。

segments.en: Very unlikely.
segments.zh: 非常不可能。

segments.en: Okay. So very good. We saw five key words there.
segments.zh: 好的。 非常好。 我们在那里看到了五个关键词。

segments.en: Let's take a break and listen to the dialogue again.
segments.zh: 让我们休息一下，再听一次对话。

segments.en: Have you read all these crazy things that are going on around the world?
segments.zh: 你看过这些世界各地的离奇传闻吗？

segments.en: What do you mean?
segments.zh: 你是什么意思？

segments.en: I was reading about how some people get tricked or drugged in their hotel rooms and have their organs removed.
segments.zh: 我看到有人说，住酒店的人可能遭人哄骗或下药，器官被摘走。

segments.en: Then they're sold on the black market.
segments.zh: 然后那些器官被拿到黑市贩卖。

segments.en: Don't tell me you actually believe all that.
segments.zh: 你不会真信这些吧？

segments.en: Don't be so gullible.
segments.zh: 不要那么轻信。

segments.en: They are just urban legends. They're just stories people make up to scare you.
segments.zh: 它们只是都市传说。 它们只是人们为了吓唬你而编造的故事。

segments.en: Well, I was also reading about how some popular songs have subliminal or even satanic messages if you play them backwards.
segments.zh: 我还看到有人说，把某些流行歌曲倒放，会听到潜意识暗示，甚至撒旦崇拜的信息。

segments.en: Can you believe that?
segments.zh: 你能信吗？

segments.en: You really think an artist or songwriter is going to go through the trouble of putting subliminal or satanic messages in a song?
segments.zh: 你真觉得歌手或词曲作者会费力往歌里藏潜意识暗示或撒旦崇拜信息？

segments.en: Don't be so naive.
segments.zh: 别这么天真。

segments.en: Well maybe you are right, but how about the story about how KFC has rows of headless chickens which are super grown in order to get bigger chickens faster?
segments.zh: 好吧，也许你是对的，但肯德基养着一排排无头鸡、让它们快速催长以便更快得到更大的鸡，这个故事又怎么说？

segments.en: Sounds a bit too farfetched to be true, don't you think?
segments.zh: 听起来太牵强了，不像是真的，你不觉得吗？

segments.en: All right, let's take a look now at a couple of phrases on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们现在看一下关于流利表达的几个短语。

segments.en: Now in Fluency Builder today we're going to start out with the story about organs, this urban legend.
segments.zh: 现在在流利表达中，我们将从关于器官的故事开始，这个都市传说。

segments.en: Now what happens when the organ is taken, the story says that it's sold on the black market.
segments.zh: 器官被摘走之后呢？故事说它会被拿到黑市上卖掉。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you probably hear this in the news or a lot of places, the black market basically.
segments.zh: 所以你可能在新闻或很多地方听到了这一点，基本上是黑市。

segments.en: It's not really a physical place, but it's where things are sold illegally.
segments.zh: 这不是一个真正的物理场所，但它是非法出售的东西。

segments.en: So guns, organs, stuff like that.
segments.zh: 所以枪支，器官，类似的东西。

segments.en: Exactly. So the black market, like you say, is not a place you can go to.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以黑市，就像你说的，不是你可以去的地方。

segments.en: It's an idea.
segments.zh: 这是一个想法。

segments.en: And it's basically anything that's illegal that's being sold. Like guns are often sold in the black market.
segments.zh: 它基本上是任何非法的东西被出售。 像枪支一样经常在黑市上出售。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Sometimes stolen cars are sold in the black market.
segments.zh: 有时被盗的汽车在黑市上出售。

segments.en: Also organs can be sold in the black market. And this is a serious problem because obviously all of this is illegal.
segments.zh: 也可以在黑市出售器官。 这是一个严重的问题，因为显然所有这些都是非法的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So the black market is where all this happens.
segments.zh: 所以黑市就是这一切发生的地方。

segments.en: Now moving on to the next urban legend that we actually didn't really talk about too much is how many people believe that popular songs have subliminal or satanic messages in them.
segments.zh: 接下来看下一个都市传说——我们其实没怎么聊过它，就是有很多人相信流行歌曲里藏着潜意识信息甚至撒旦信息。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So let's take a look at the word subliminal first. We all know what a message is, right?
segments.zh: 所以先来看 subliminal 这个词。message 我们都知道是什么意思，对吧？

segments.en: It's something that's told to us.
segments.zh: 这是告诉我们的。

segments.en: But a subliminal message is something that is told to us without us knowing.
segments.zh: 但潜意识信息是在我们不知情的情况下告诉我们的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it goes into your mind, but you don't even know it.
segments.zh: 所以它进入了你的脑海，但你甚至不知道。

segments.en: So it's something that a lot of people believe in because they think that marketing people or big businesses are trying to control our behavior.
segments.zh: 所以这是很多人相信的事情，因为他们认为营销人员或大企业正试图控制我们的行为。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So I could say very quietly, Marco, buy me dinner.
segments.zh: 所以我可以小声地说：马可，请我吃晚饭。

segments.en: And that's a subliminal message.
segments.zh: 这是一个潜意识的信息。

segments.en: Marco says, hey, I was thinking about getting everyone dinner tonight.
segments.zh: 马可说，嘿，我正想着今晚请大家吃晚饭呢。

segments.en: And then that's basically a way to control your actions. And so whether or not this is possible, that's another discussion.
segments.zh: 然后这基本上是一种控制你的行为的方式。 所以这是否可能，这是另一个讨论。

segments.en: That's another discussion.
segments.zh: 这是另一个讨论。

segments.en: But so, yeah, that's basically what a lot of people say that some TV commercials or ads have these subliminal messages that are trying to convince you or persuade you into maybe consuming that product.
segments.zh: 但是，是的，这基本上就是很多人所说的一些电视广告或广告具有这些潜意识信息，这些信息试图说服您或说服您可能消费该产品。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: But they're a little bit different from satanic messages.
segments.zh: 但它们与撒旦的信息有点不同。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So that's basically dealing with Satan or the devil.
segments.zh: 所以这基本上是与撒旦或魔鬼打交道。

segments.en: That's right. So the idea that there are satanic messages means that they're messages about the devil, about how maybe God does not exist or like, you know, that you should do evil, not good.
segments.zh: 没错。所以所谓有撒旦信息，就是这些信息关于魔鬼，比如说上帝并不存在，或者你知道，叫你去作恶而不是行善。

segments.en: So they're very dark and very kind of angry messages.
segments.zh: 所以他们是非常黑暗和非常愤怒的信息。

segments.en: I think they talk about, for example, I'm not sure which song it is, but like by Ozzy Osbourne that if you play it backwards, supposedly there's this message that says, you know, worship the devil and stuff like that. So that's where these urban legends come from.
segments.zh: 我记得他们举的例子，具体是哪首歌我不确定，好像是 Ozzy Osbourne 的，据说你要是倒着放，里面就有个信息说，你知道，去崇拜魔鬼之类的。这些都市传说就是这么来的。

segments.en: But obviously it's either coincidence or not true.
segments.zh: 但显然这要么是巧合，要么不是真的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we've got these messages that are also an urban legend.
segments.zh: 所以这些信息也属于都市传说。

segments.en: But the final one is about KFC.
segments.zh: 但最后一个传说是关于肯德基的。

segments.en: So KFC would be Kentucky Fried Chicken.
segments.zh: 所以肯德基会是肯塔基炸鸡。

segments.en: And what is the legend?
segments.zh: 什么是传说？

segments.en: The legend is about their food.
segments.zh: 传说是关于他们的食物。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: They say that they don't really have real chickens. Well, they take chickens and they just super grow them. The chickens are super grown in order for them to get bigger and faster.
segments.zh: 他们说他们用的不是真正的鸡。他们拿鸡来，对它们进行超级催长。这些鸡被超级催长，就是为了让它们长得更大、更快。

segments.en: And that's basically that they don't even really have heads. They just have some hoses that go into their bodies and feed them.
segments.zh: 这基本上是说它们甚至没有真正的头，只是插几根软管进身体里喂它们。

segments.en: And in four weeks you have a chicken.
segments.zh: 四个星期后你有一只鸡。

segments.en: That's disgusting. That's disgusting. The idea is super grown chickens. And so they're basically they're not real chickens.
segments.zh: 那太恶心了。那太恶心了。这个说法就是这些鸡是被超级催大的。所以它们基本上不算真正的鸡。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's what the legend says is that they're not.
segments.zh: 这就是传说中的说法，他们不是。

segments.en: I mean, they really are, but they're not like naturally grown. You know, usually a chicken takes three months to grow or something.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，它们确实是鸡，但不是自然长成的。你知道，一般一只鸡要长三个月左右。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: That's disgusting. I don't want to talk about that.
segments.zh: 那很恶心。 我不想谈论那个。

segments.en: But the idea of super growing is like using chemicals to do something that's not natural.
segments.zh: 但超级成长的想法就像使用化学物质来做一些不自然的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Chemicals or hormones and stuff. So that's they use it, for example, on plants. You can super grow a plant by adding fertilizer and vitamins and stuff to the soil that makes it grow faster.
segments.zh: 化学物质或激素之类的东西。比如他们会把它用在植物上。往土壤里加肥料、维生素之类的，就能让植物超级生长，长得更快。

segments.en: Or maybe you have bigger carrots than normal, bigger potatoes because they're super grown.
segments.zh: 或者，也许你的胡萝卜比平时更大，土豆更大，因为它们是超级生长的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, all right.
segments.zh: 那好吧。

segments.en: That's a lot of great stuff.
segments.zh: 这是很多很棒的东西。

segments.en: Let's take a listen to the dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 让我们最后一次听一听对话。

segments.en: Have you read all these crazy things that are going on around the world?
segments.zh: 你看过这些世界各地的离奇传闻吗？

segments.en: What do you mean?
segments.zh: 你是什么意思？

segments.en: I was reading about how some people get tricked or drugged in their hotel rooms and have their organs removed.
segments.zh: 我看到有人说，住酒店的人可能遭人哄骗或下药，器官被摘走。

segments.en: Then they're sold on the black market.
segments.zh: 然后那些器官被拿到黑市贩卖。

segments.en: Don't tell me you actually believe all that.
segments.zh: 你不会真信这些吧？

segments.en: Don't be so gullible. They are just urban legends. They're just stories people make up to scare you.
segments.zh: 别这么轻信，那只是都市传说，都是人们编出来吓人的。

segments.en: Well, I was also reading about how some popular songs have subliminal or even satanic messages if you play them backwards.
segments.zh: 我还看到有人说，把某些流行歌曲倒放，会听到潜意识暗示，甚至撒旦崇拜的信息。

segments.en: Can you believe that?
segments.zh: 你能信吗？

segments.en: You really think an artist or songwriter is going to go through the trouble of putting subliminal or satanic messages in a song?
segments.zh: 你真觉得歌手或词曲作者会费力往歌里藏潜意识暗示或撒旦崇拜信息？

segments.en: Don't be so naive.
segments.zh: 别这么天真。

segments.en: Well, maybe you are right.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许你是对的。

segments.en: But how about the story about how KFC has rows of headless chickens which are super grown in order to get bigger chickens faster?
segments.zh: 可传说肯德基养着一排排无头鸡，让它们迅速长大，好更快得到大块鸡肉，这又怎么说？

segments.en: Sounds a bit too far-fetched to be true, don't you think?
segments.zh: 听起来也太离谱了，你不觉得吗？

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, all these urban legends, they are obviously most of them, if not all of them, are untrue. But they're very popular.
segments.zh: 所以，所有这些都市传说，它们显然是其中的大部分，如果不是全部的话，都是不真实的。 但它们非常受欢迎。

segments.en: Why do you think that is?
segments.zh: 为什么你认为这是？

segments.en: I think people like to believe these stories. They're gossipy.
segments.zh: 我认为人们喜欢相信这些故事。它们很适合拿来八卦。

segments.en: They're scary.
segments.zh: 它们很吓人。

segments.en: You get to make your friends kind of nervous about stuff. But I think also we don't trust a lot of these things because we've heard for years and years and years and years about subliminal messages and marketing strategies or about these kind of hidden messages in songs.
segments.zh: 你可以让你的朋友为一些事情紧张。但我觉得，我们之所以不太信这些，是因为很多很多年来一直听到关于潜意识信息、营销策略，或者歌曲里这类隐藏信息的说法。

segments.en: So, there's part of us that wants to believe them.
segments.zh: 所以，我们内心有一部分是愿意相信它们的。

segments.en: But the other part is that you hear it enough, you start to believe it.
segments.zh: 但另一部分是你听得够多，你开始相信它。

segments.en: Because I was reading up on a couple of them and the most recent ones are about how they make the connection about how Nostradamus predicted the 9-11 incident or how Coca-Cola is actually the one that invented Santa Claus.
segments.zh: 因为我查了其中几个，最近的一些说法是把诺查丹玛斯预言 9·11 事件、或者说圣诞老人其实是可口可乐发明的这些联系到一起。

segments.en: And even this KFC one where people just believe a lot of different things.
segments.zh: 即使是这个肯德基一家，人们只是相信很多不同的东西。

segments.en: I even found one, the urban legend about be careful when you go to the movie theater because there might be a syringe or something on the seat that if you sit down it infects you with AIDS or something like this.
segments.zh: 我甚至发现了一个都市传说，说去电影院要小心，座位上可能有注射器之类的东西，你一坐下去就会染上艾滋病或类似的东西。

segments.en: So, there's so many of them out there that if you think about it, they don't even really make sense.
segments.zh: 所以这类传说太多了，你仔细想想，它们根本说不通。

segments.en: They don't.
segments.zh: 确实说不通。

segments.en: And I understand that sometimes there'll be one news story like about a needle in a candy box.
segments.zh: 我知道有时会有一个新闻报道，比如糖果盒中的针。

segments.en: And all of a sudden people say, well, don't eat candy because there's needles in candy boxes.
segments.zh: 突然间，人们说，好吧，不要吃糖果，因为糖果盒里有针。

segments.en: And obviously, one time event turns into this massive kind of craze.
segments.zh: 显然，一次事件变成了这种巨大的热潮。

segments.en: Yeah. But it is interesting, especially with this whole topic of subliminal messages. I do remember that actually there was a marketing campaign that was banned in movie theaters when the previews before the actual movie came on.
segments.zh: 是的。不过这很有趣，尤其是说到潜意识信息这个话题。我记得确实有个营销活动，因为在电影正片放映前的预告时段播放，被电影院禁掉了。

segments.en: Supposedly, they had the sound or maybe on the screen somebody opening up a Coke can and the smell of Coke actually coming into the theater.
segments.zh: 据说，他们会播放声音，或者屏幕上有人打开一罐可乐，可乐的气味真的会飘进影院。

segments.en: And that was kind of like subliminal marketing making people want to go get a Coke.
segments.zh: 这有点像潜意识营销让人们想去买可乐。

segments.en: Definitely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: Well, we used to pump the exhaust from the popcorn maker when I worked in a movie theater throughout the lobby. So, everyone smells it and it smells so good. Everyone wants to buy it.
segments.zh: 我在电影院工作的时候，会把爆米花机排出的香气抽到整个大厅。这样每个人都能闻到，而且闻起来特别香，大家都想买。

segments.en: You want to buy popcorn?
segments.zh: 你想买爆米花吗？

segments.en: Oh, yeah. We would totally use that.
segments.zh: 哦，是的。 我们会完全使用它。

segments.en: So, yeah.
segments.zh: 所以，对。

segments.en: That is a way of like, I guess it is subliminal because you're not directly telling them to buy it, but you are just giving them all the...
segments.zh: 这算是一种方式吧，我想这属于潜意识，因为你没有直接叫他们买，只是把所有的……

segments.en: Adjusting it through audio or visual or oratory cues.
segments.zh: 通过声音、画面或口头暗示来引导。

segments.en: Right. And then you have the opportunity to sell them the most expensive popcorn they'll ever buy.
segments.zh: 对。然后你就有机会卖给他们这辈子买过最贵的爆米花。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Twelve dollars for a bag of popcorn.
segments.zh: 一袋爆米花十二美元。

segments.en: All right. So, it is a very interesting topic.
segments.zh: 好的。 所以，这是一个非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: Let us know if you have any comments or questions about it.
segments.zh: 如果您对此有任何意见或问题，请告诉我们。

segments.en: You can find us at EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 您可以在 EnglishPod.com 找到我们。

segments.en: We hope to see you guys there. Bye.
segments.zh: 我们希望在那里见到你们。 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
